key_insight: The paper combines POD model reduction with high-order multiscale reconstruction to make transient multi-continuum fracture/porous-media simulations much cheaper while preserving HOMS-level accuracy and oscillatory detail.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster large-scale 2D/3D simulations of fractured and highly heterogeneous media, which is valuable for subsurface flow, transport, and damage-related multiphysics applications.
method: Build a vector-valued POD space from snapshots of the coupled homogenized multi-continuum system.
Project the block homogenized equations onto a low-dimensional reduced basis.
Use either online HOMS reassembly or offline corrected-basis reconstruction with recovered value, gradient, exchange, second-derivative, and time-derivative terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical error estimates and numerical tests in two- and three-dimensional heterogeneous cases showing reduced solutions preserve HOMS accuracy and local oscillations while lowering cost.
watch_item: Performance depends on the representativeness of POD snapshots and the overhead of constructing/applying corrected bases for new parameter regimes or long-time dynamics.
paper_title: POD-accelerated high-order multiscale method with corrected-basis reconstruction for transient multi-continuum problems
